title: Review: Polarisation; Electromagnetic spectrum; Reflection and refraction; Total internal reflection and optical fibres; Lenses
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: W04-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; W05-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; W05-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; W03-1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: W02-1#N.2, W04-1#N.9a, W05-1#N.3a, W13-1#N.8b, W02-1#N.14, W04-1#N.6a, W05-1#N.14a, W13-1#N.10, W05-1#N.5a, W13-1#N.9. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Ray
items.clue: Line perpendicular to the wavefronts, showing the direction the energy travels.

items.label: Critical angle
items.clue: Incidence, measured from the normal, at which the refracted beam runs along the boundary.

items.label: Total internal reflection
items.clue: Beyond a certain incidence, no light passes into the lower-n medium: all of it bounces back.

items.label: Longitudinal wave
items.clue: Has oscillations along the direction of travel, so only one oscillation direction is possible.

questions.stem: Predict first. Which statement describes the nature of electromagnetic waves?

options.text: Oscillations of the particles of the medium they travel through, so they cannot cross a vacuum
Oscillating electric and magnetic fields that travel faster in a vacuum the higher their frequency
Streams of tiny charged particles given out by the source, which can travel through a vacuum
Oscillating electric and magnetic fields, perpendicular to each other and to the direction of travel

questions.stem: A ray of light passes from air into a transparent liquid. The incident ray makes an angle of 40.0° with the surface of the liquid and the refracted ray makes an angle of 55.0° with the surface. The speed of light in air is 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. What is the speed of light in the liquid?
Light can cross a flat boundary between water (n = 1.33) and glass (n = 1.50) in either direction. Which statement about total internal reflection at this boundary is correct?

options.text: It can occur for light in the glass heading towards the water.
It can occur for light that is in the water and heading towards the glass.
It can occur for light going either way, if the angle is large enough.
It needs air beyond the boundary, so it does not occur at this one.

questions.explanation: Total internal reflection needs light heading into a lower refractive index: here, light in the glass (1.50) meeting the water (1.33), at angles of incidence above sin⁻¹(1.33/1.50), about 62°.

questions.stem: An object is placed 24.0 cm from a thin diverging lens whose focal length has a magnitude of 12.0 cm. Using the real-is-positive convention, what is the image distance v?
In a vacuum, the microwaves in a speed camera have a wavelength of 3.0 cm, and the light from a yellow lamp has a wavelength of 600 nm. How do their frequencies compare?

options.text: The microwave frequency is 5 × 10⁴ times the light frequency, since f rises with λ.
They are equal, because both waves travel at the same speed, c, in a vacuum.
The light frequency is 5 × 10⁴ times the microwave frequency, since f = c/λ.
The light frequency is higher, because light travels faster than microwaves.

questions.explanation: Same c for both, so f ∝ 1/λ. Ratio = (3.0 × 10⁻² m)/(600 × 10⁻⁹ m) = 5 × 10⁴: the light's frequency is that many times higher.

questions.stem: The refractive index of a certain plastic is 1.5. Which statement correctly describes what this value means?

options.text: Light travels 1.5 times as fast in the plastic as in a vacuum.
The plastic's density is 1.5 times the density of water.
A ray entering from air is bent to 1/1.5 of its angle of incidence.
Light travels 1.5 times as fast in a vacuum as it does in the plastic.

questions.stem: An optical fibre has a glass core of refractive index 1.50, surrounded by glass of refractive index 1.40. On a straight stretch, a ray meets the core's wall at 75° to the normal. Where the fibre bends, the same ray meets the wall at 66° to the normal. What happens at each point?

options.text: Trapped at both: once light is inside the core, it cannot leave.
Totally internally reflected at 75°; at 66° some light passes out of the core.
Totally internally reflected at both, as both angles are more than 41.8°.
Some light passes out at 75°, but the ray is trapped at 66°.

questions.explanation: The critical angle is sin⁻¹(1.40/1.50) = 69.0°. 75° > 69.0°: TIR. 66° < 69.0°: part of the light refracts out (at 78° to the normal). A sharp bend lets light leak.

questions.stem: A projector has a thin converging lens of focal length 8.0 cm. A slide is placed 9.0 cm from the lens, close to it. Which describes the image?

options.text: Virtual, upright, 8 times larger, 72 cm from the lens
Real, inverted, 8 times larger, 72 cm from the lens
Real, inverted, smaller, 4.2 cm from the lens
Real, upright, 8 times larger, 72 cm from the lens

questions.explanation: The slide is outside F, so the rays really meet: real and inverted. Image distance: 1/(1/8.0 − 1/9.0) = 72 cm; magnification 72/9.0 = 8. That is why a projector's slide goes in upside down.

questions.stem: A glass block of refractive index 1.52 is under water of refractive index 1.33. A ray inside the glass meets the glass–water boundary at an angle of incidence of 55.0°. What happens to the ray?

options.text: It is totally internally reflected, as 55.0° is more than 41.1°.
It refracts into the water at 69.4° to the normal.
It refracts into the water at 45.8° to the normal.
It passes into the water at 55.0°, without bending.

questions.explanation: The critical angle is sin⁻¹(1.33/1.52) = 61.0°, and 55.0° < 61.0°, so it refracts: 1.52 sin 55.0° = 1.33 sin θ₂, θ₂ = 69.4°.

questions.stem: An object 3.0 cm tall is placed 30.0 cm from a thin converging lens of focal length 20.0 cm. What is the height of the image?

options.text: 1.5 cm
6.0 cm
1.2 cm
2.0 cm
